title: Cells of each kind vary little about a mean size, whatever the body size

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cells of each kind vary little about a mean size, whatever the body size

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Cells of each kind vary little about a characteristic mean size and have absolute size limits, so dwarf and giant individuals of a species (e.g. Crepidula, sea-urchin larvae) differ in cell number rather than cell size.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: An immediate and remarkable result of the principles just described is a tendency on the part of all cells, according to their kind, to vary but little about a certain mean size, and to have, in fact, certain absolute limitations of magnitude.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter II, “On Magnitude”; topic “Fixed cell size”. Scope: tissue cells of animals, compared across individuals of different body size

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch02-16: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The variables and refuting pattern are clear, and extensive cellular images exist. However, data directly pairing individual body size, cell size and cell number across the claimed taxa and phenotypes are incomplete, so the broad law is only partially resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure volumes of matched cell types across dwarf, normal and giant individuals and regress cell size and cell number on body size. Nearly invariant cell size with number accounting for body-size differences supports the claim; strong within-type cell-size scaling refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Some tissues vary by ploidy or hypertrophy.

Matched body-size phenotypes and cell types are uncommon in one dataset.

Cell volume estimates depend on tissue preparation and segmentation.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.8
operationalizability: 0.9
data existence: 0.65
data adequacy: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cell size versus cell number is a clean partition, and both quantities are routine to analyse once tabulated. Existing compilations and images cover enough mammalian and model tissues for a strong subset test, but not the claim's full scope of every cell kind across dwarf and giant animals. Building that table is a months-scale harmonization, so the claim is partly resolvable now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For each cell type, compare the spread of cell size with the spread of body size across dwarf and giant individuals or related species, and partition the body-size difference into cell size versus cell number. The claim is confirmed if cell size stays in a narrow band and cell number accounts for body size; it is refuted if homologous cells scale up with the body.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Polyploid and hypertrophic tissues are real exceptions and have to be separated by cell class.

Public sizes are dense for a few tissues and model species, not for the Crepidula and urchin cases named.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.5
data existence: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.85
discriminating power: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.55
